title: Sell Mineral Rights in Ault, CO
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Ault, CO
metaDescription: Ault sits in core northern Weld County Wattenberg acreage. See how nearby Niobrara-Codell horizontal units affect what your mineral or royalty interest is worth.
heroLead: Ault is a small farm town in northern Weld County sitting inside some of the most consistently drilled acreage in the Wattenberg Field.
intro: Operators have run multi-well horizontal pads throughout this part of Weld County for well over a decade, targeting the Niobrara and Codell benches with laterals that regularly stretch a mile or more. If you hold minerals tied to a legal description near Ault, there's a real chance they sit inside an existing production unit even if you've never received a check — units get expanded and re-pooled as new wells come online.

sections.heading: Why this part of Weld County stays active
paragraphs: The rock quality in the Wattenberg core around Ault has kept it a priority area for operators even as commodity prices have swung over the past decade. Multi-well pad development lets a single surface location reach minerals under a wide area, which is one reason a tract that's never had a well physically sited on it can still be pooled into a paying unit.

sections.heading: Farm-family ownership and old leases
paragraphs: A lot of the mineral ownership around Ault traces back to farm families who've held the land, or just the minerals, for generations. Original leases signed decades ago sometimes get renewed or replaced as new operators pick up acreage, and it's not unusual for an owner to lose track of which company currently holds the lease. We check operator-of-record filings with the state directly rather than relying on old paperwork alone.

sections.heading: What a decline curve looks like on a core Wattenberg well
paragraphs: A horizontal Niobrara-Codell well in this part of Weld County typically produces the bulk of its lifetime volume in the first two to three years before settling into a long, lower-volume tail. If your family's minerals have been in a unit for a while, your royalty checks have probably already dropped from an early peak, which is normal and doesn't mean the well is failing — it's simply following the expected curve for this type of completion.

faqs.question: How do I know if my Ault-area minerals are in a producing unit?
faqs.answer: We check current unit boundaries and permit filings against your legal description. Because this is core Wattenberg acreage, the odds are meaningfully better than in most other parts of the state.

faqs.question: My lease is decades old — is it still valid?
faqs.answer: It depends on whether the lease has been held by production or has expired. We review the lease terms and current operator filings as part of any offer.

faqs.question: Do you buy interests that have never produced?
faqs.answer: Yes, particularly in a high-activity area like Ault, where we price against realistic development odds even without a production history yet.

faqs.question: My checks have dropped a lot since the well first started — is that normal?
faqs.answer: Yes. Horizontal Niobrara-Codell wells decline sharply in the first couple of years before leveling into a longer, lower-volume stretch. We factor the well's current position on that curve into any offer.
